Bug_Title: EI2: May expose internal representation by creating a buffer which incorporates reference to array (EI_EXPOSE_BUF2)
Bug_Details:
This code creates a buffer which stores a reference to an external array or the array of an external buffer into
the internal representation of the object. 
 If instances
 are accessed by untrusted code, and unchecked changes to
 the array would compromise security or other
 important properties, you will need to do something different.
Storing a copy of the array is a better approach in many situations.
Bug_Explanation: The constructor of the BuggyBuffer class directly assigns the input array to its private field 'buffer'. This exposes the internal representation of the object by storing a reference to the external array.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case modifies the input array after creating the BuggyBuffer object. Since the BuggyBuffer class directly assigns the input array to its private field 'buffer', any changes made to the input array will be reflected in the BuggyBuffer object. This triggers the EI2 bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test modifies the input array after creating the BuggyBuffer object, which stores a reference to the input array. This modification is reflected in the result array returned by the showBug() method, indicating that the internal representation of the BuggyBuffer object is exposed.
